chapter: Gabriel's sons, small bands and Detroit
title: Teaching his sons trumpet and leading a big band
summary: Gabriel teaches his sons Morton and August trumpet using what he learned from old man Delmore, and runs a big band with his sons and nephew.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Later on it got to the point, I didn't help all them fellas on the trumpet I got out the band with. I couldn't get no trumpet players at all. They stick with me. Right up. So anyhow, what I did, I take in and... So I said I'm going to break my boys in on the trumpet. And I know they got to play with me whether they want or not. Because I'm the daddy. So I take in Morton and August. And I learned down the trumpet, how to play the trumpet. And I learned trumpet from old man Delmore. And August and Mauret, I often find all the artificial fingering. They call it artificial but it's all in the book. Yeah. And they make all them fingering three, four ways. I know all that. So he taught old man Delmore. So anyhow, I learned about them. I broke them and I learned the trumpet. Every day I'd have them practicing them running over and making them write their music. So I had my own trumpets. So then I had a big band and about... Boy went to war when he... Before he went to war, I had a big band and I had my little nephew, Clowns Ford. Do you know him?
I've heard of him. He plays with Fat Domino.

Of course he's a progressive, you know. He's not. So I had him in the band and my little boy Charles Gabriel in the band playing tenor. August playing trumpet three boys. August and Mauret. And then I used him in the brass band. I had this boy, Herbert Horace, playing high note and Henry. Henry Jarvis, he was playing tenor. I would play the Alpes, so that was four. But Alpes could play clarinet, but that Henry Jarvis, we had three clarinets we played. He could play the tenor, he couldn't play the clarinet. But about 16th piece, I used Richard McLean on the bass. Oh yeah. I used him on the banjo piano. I didn't even use this boy, Winley's brother. Not Winley the other one, Homer. Oh yeah. Homer Eugene.
